items.title: Bill Huntington and Charlie Suhor Interview, 1992-04-06
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...Earl Palmer was playing at the Texas Lounge on Canal Street with Earl Williams I think it was... [INTERVIEWEE] Another great innovator. Yes. Very important, very important guy.

ctx.x: Or you can talk about venues, too, so we can get some feeling of where modern jazz players might have been able to play. How exceptional it was for them to get in front of the public. Were they playing for themselves? Were they playing for general audiences? Right.

A lot of that stuff is chronicled on record in the sixties in my Down B columns, which I'll be donating shortly, so that you'll have the venues, the artists, and changes in personnel. Of course that doesn't give you the interpretive stuff and who were the spiritual and musical leaders. Yeah, that's important. So Mouse played in little quarter dungeons, little back rooms and quarters and places like that. Blackwell we used to have a place called Dante's Inferno in the quarter, and little jazz clubs, Holes in the…
Another great innovator. Yes. Very important, very important guy.
